solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Insect identified by most of the instances of clothing damage

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it bar its last letter, so the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: the word taken as written before trimming
rips are tears in clothes

explanation.surface: An insect is named as the culprit behind holes in someone's clothes, like a moth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims THE to TH. The surface points at moths, but thrips are tiny plant-eating insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrips are tiny winged bugs, a kind of insect that feeds on plants.

clue.text: Agony amid dreadful toil? The stock-in-trade of many an artist

definitions.text: The stock-in-trade of many an artist

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other
dreadful suggests something badly made, so the letters of toil are rearranged

parts.note: agony is extreme pain

explanation.surface: Suffering in the middle of awful labour is the lot of many a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agony' and 'toil' paint a scene of hardship; the definition is the whole second sentence about an artist's materials.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters' pigment ground in linseed is a main working material for many artists, hence their stock-in-trade.

clue.text: Plain ramshackle loo, still receiving treatment externally

indicators.note: externally means on the outside, so the longer piece wraps round the shorter

parts.note: someone still being treated is not yet cured, so uncured

indicators.note: ramshackle means falling apart, so the letters of loo are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plain, tumbledown toilet is still being repaired, on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still receiving treatment' means not yet healed; 'ramshackle' signals the anagram and 'externally' the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain has no added tint or embellishment, a synonym in the sense of undyed or unadorned.

clue.text: Show respect to Greece's foremost elite, stifling rising amusement

indicators.note: foremost asks for the first letter of Greece
stifling means smothering, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: the elect are a chosen elite

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: amusement is fun

explanation.surface: Greece's top people are honoured while they suppress growing laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reads upward in a down light; 'stifling' places the turned word inside, and 'foremost' takes one initial.
explanation.definitionFit: To bend the knee is a traditional gesture of reverence, so it means to show respect.

clue.text: Goddess — and the best mark she'll give?

parts.note: the mark she'll give is her mark, giving the word her
A is the top grade on a school report

explanation.surface: A goddess is asked what top grade she might hand out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as HER A: her A-grade, the best mark she would award.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera is the queen of the Greek gods, wife of Zeus, so a goddess.

clue.text: Child, I note, following soldier

parts.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so ant stands for soldier

explanation.surface: A child writes a note after a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like a link word placing pieces, but it gives F, the abbreviation used in page references.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby or very young child is an infant, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Man, perhaps, standing up on new rock in theatrical location

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an example of an isle
ore is metal-bearing rock

explanation.surface: A man stands on a fresh rock somewhere in a play's setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man, perhaps' is the Isle of Man, an isle; 'standing up' turns ISLE into ELSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore is the Danish castle where Shakespeare sets Hamlet, a famous stage setting.

clue.text: Head covering that's ruined in the rain

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of the rain are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hat or scarf gets spoiled by a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' shuffles the seven letters of THE RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine mesh worn to keep hair in place is worn on the head, so it covers it.

clue.text: Record the fifth source of water?

parts.note: a tap is a source of water
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A question about logging a fifth spring.
explanation.definitionFit: To tape is to record sound or video onto magnetic tape.

clue.text: Sea creature heading off to eat seabird at all times

indicators.note: to eat means to take in, so one piece swallows the other
heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a seal is a sea creature
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A marine animal sets off to feed on a gull-like bird, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea creature' and 'seabird' both look like the definition; it is 'at all times', with 'heading off' and 'to eat' as the signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting exists forever, so it holds always, at every moment.

clue.text: I'm ready to go to University at a moment's notice

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
prompt means ready and quick to act

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are all set to head off to college at short notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done off the cuff, without preparation, is done on the spur of the moment.

clue.text: Doctor about to snatch this violin? That's dramatic

indicators.note: to snatch means to take away, so letters are removed from the word dramatic

parts.note: c. for circa is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: A doctor is about to grab a violin, and the speaker remarks how theatrical that is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to snatch' removes DR from the front of DRAMATIC and C from its end. 'That's dramatic' looks like a comment but holds the word worked on.
explanation.definitionFit: Amati was a family of Cremona luthiers, so an Amati is a violin made by them.

clue.text: Irish location's second language not given name

indicators.note: not given means left out, so a letter is taken from the word for language

parts.note: lingo is an informal word for a language

explanation.surface: An Irish place's second tongue goes unnamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not given' drops N from LINGO, leaving LIGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a town and county in north-west Ireland, so a place there.

clue.text: The Parisian gets very hot after running in part of Africa

parts.note: le is French for the
so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: running suggests something set in motion and jumbled, so the letters of hot are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Frenchman becomes overheated after a jog somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after running' looks like a time phrase but signals the anagram; 'The Parisian' means French for the.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa, so a country of that continent.

clue.text: Various Gaels, circling rising ground, encountering hard weapon

indicators.note: circling means going round, so one piece surrounds another
various suggests different arrangements, so the letters of Gaels are rearranged

parts.note: a hill is ground that rises
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A band of Irish or Scots go round a hill and meet a tough weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' signals the anagram and 'circling' the wrapping; 'rising ground' is simply a description of a hill, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A shillelagh is an Irish cudgel of blackthorn, so a weapon.

clue.text: Oscar's condition around Tuesday — briefly tense?

indicators.note: around means placed about, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: state means condition
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An Academy Award winner's state of mind around Tuesday is a little edgy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the wrapping; 'briefly' applies to both the day and the grammar term, each shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is the small gold figure handed out as a film award, a small figurine.

clue.text: It contains an expanse of white and is enough to make art critic cancel

definitions.text: It contains an expanse of white

indicators.note: the letters given are just enough to make something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: A frozen polar zone is such a blank sight that a reviewer would call off the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enough to make' rearranges ART CRITIC CANCEL, fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar line round Antarctica encloses a vast area of snow and ice, a white expanse.

clue.text: Liking copy that includes little for Sarkozy

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to ape is to copy
petit is French for little, Sarkozy being a former French president

explanation.surface: A fondness for imitation that takes in a small word from a French president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that includes' signals the wrapping; Nicolas Sarkozy was President of France, so his word for little is French.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetite for something is a taste or desire for it, a fondness.

clue.text: Escort vessel — check last of ballast in centre

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the pieces go inside the word for centre

parts.note: the core is the centre
to vet is to check

indicators.note: last of asks for the final letter of ballast

explanation.surface: A navy escort ship has its ballast inspected amidships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the insertion and 'last of' takes one letter; 'centre' gives the outer piece, not a middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A corvette is a small warship used to escort convoys.

clue.text: Praise encountered in part of theatre?

definitions.text: Praise encountered in part of theatre?

indicators.note: encountered in means found within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the pit is the area in front of the stage
laud means praise

explanation.surface: Applause heard in the stalls area of a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encountered in' signals the insertion. The whole clue is also the definition: acclaim heard from the audience below the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of approval, the kind of acclaim heard from an audience.

clue.text: Very worried Force will interrupt a heist

indicators.note: interrupt means break into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a raid is a robbery or heist
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious that the police force will burst in on a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will interrupt' puts F inside A RAID, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone scared is frightened, which is strong worry.

clue.text: Exotic creature taking tips from flower-seller

indicators.note: taking the tips means removing the end letters

parts.note: a florist sells flowers

explanation.surface: An unusual animal pinches tips from a florist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking tips from' removes F and T, the outer letters of FLORIST. 'tips' tempts as gratuities.
explanation.definitionFit: The loris is a slow-moving primate of South and South-East Asia, an unusual animal.

clue.text: Surgical treatment certain to restrict two regular members of United

indicators.note: restrict means to hem in, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: two letters picked at a regular interval from United, every third letter

explanation.surface: A sure-fire operation keeps two of United's regular players in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two regular members of' takes the 1st and 4th letters of UNITED, U and T, and 'to restrict' puts SURE round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitching a wound closed is a surgical procedure, and the stitch itself is called a suture.

clue.text: A fanatic regarding muscle development?

definitions.meaning: an enthusiast or fan of something
an informal word for muscular and well toned

explanation.surface: An enthusiast for bodybuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: Buff means both an enthusiast (a film buff) and, informally, a toned muscular physique.

clue.text: Light to start to reillumine church

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of reillumine

explanation.surface: Instructions to light a lamp to bring a church's glow back.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-held lamp or flaming brand gives illumination, a source of light.

clue.text: Commencement of hostilities, also known as a war dance

indicators.note: commencement means beginning, so the first letter of hostilities

explanation.surface: At the outbreak of fighting comes a dance performed before battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The haka is a Maori ceremonial dance, famously performed by New Zealand rugby teams before matches.

clue.text: Agitated farm animal that is caught in snarled net

indicators.note: caught in means trapped inside, so pieces go within the other
snarled means tangled, so the letters of net are rearranged

parts.note: a bull is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A worked-up bull gets trapped in a tangled net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snarled' signals the anagram and 'caught in' the insertion; 'Agitated' looks like an anagram signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullient means bubbling over with energy, so excited or worked up.

clue.text: Henry brought in permit to enter copse

indicators.note: brought in means put inside, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: a ticket admits the holder
H is the physics symbol for the henry, a unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry is let in with a pass into a small wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' puts H inside TICKET, after T.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense clump of shrubs and small trees is a small wood.

clue.text: Cargo boat not about to become military craft

indicators.note: not means without, so letters are removed from the word for a cargo boat

parts.note: a freighter carries cargo
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A cargo ship isn't about to turn into a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not about to become' reads as one phrase, but 'not' is the deletion signal, 'about' the letters removed and 'to become' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A combat aircraft is a warplane, a craft of the armed forces.
